courses.title: Kids 6–7: first English term
courses.about: 20 lessons in 3 units (All About Me, My World, Fun and Celebrations), plus 3 bonus lessons.

items.title: How the lessons work
items.body:
20 one-hour lessons for a 6–7-year-old beginner whose main language is French, two a week: one calmer lesson at home to introduce the words, one at school with games and running. Lessons are numbered, so if one is missed, carry on with the next.

### The lesson routine (60 min)
Every lesson follows the same seven steps. Each lesson below tells you exactly what to do in each step.
1. **Hello routine (5 min).** Same every time: wave, sing a short hello chant, ask "How are you?", high five. A fixed opening helps her feel safe and switch into English.
2. **Review (5–10 min).** A quick game with the last lesson's words.
3. **New words (10 min).** Show the picture card or real object, say the word three times, and have her repeat it in a loud voice, a whisper, and a silly voice. Never more than 7 new words.
4. **Movement game (10–15 min).** She answers by running, jumping, touching or pointing.
5. **Calm activity (10 min).** Coloring, drawing, a craft or matching, while you give instructions in English.
6. **Her turn to speak (5–10 min).** A role swap, puppet talk or question game where she says the words herself.
7. **Goodbye routine (5 min).** A sticker on her chart, then "Goodbye! See you Saturday!"

### Classroom English to use every lesson
Use these with gestures from day one. She will learn them without being taught: Sit down. Stand up. Look. Listen. Point to… Show me… Give me… My turn. Your turn. Again! Good job! Well done! Come here. Let's go!

### Tips for teaching a 6-year-old
- Change activity every 8–10 minutes. Her attention span is short, and that is normal.
- Speak English with gestures, pictures and real objects. Use French only for a quick rescue when she is lost.
- Don't push her to talk early. Understanding comes before speaking, so praise every attempt.
- Recycle old words in new lessons: count the animals, name the colors of clothes.
- End every lesson on a game she is good at, so she leaves proud.

### Materials kit (make once, reuse all term)
- **Picture cards:** printed from each lesson's file (see Printing below).
- **A puppet or stuffed toy** that "only speaks English." The Lesson 1 file has a monkey puppet to cut out. Give it a name; she will talk to it more easily than to you.
- **Crayons, child-safe scissors, tape, plain paper.**
- **A soft ball and a "mystery bag"** (any cloth bag to hide objects in).
- **A star chart** from the Lesson 1 file: she colors one star per lesson.
- **A folder** to keep her drawings and crafts. Show it to her parents at the end.
Each lesson ends with a **home practice** idea for her parents: 2–3 words or one phrase to use with her during the week.

### Printing
Every lesson has its own file, named like "Lesson 03 printables.pdf." Print it on your hard paper a day or two before class, then cut on the dashed lines. Each lesson below says exactly which pages are in its file.
- **Total:** 45 sheets for Lessons 1–20, plus 5 for the bonus lessons.
- **Paper size:** A4. If your printer uses Letter paper, choose "Fit to page."
- **Color:** picture cards, the puppet, the weather wheel and the games look best in color. Worksheets are fine in black and white.
- **Keep the cards:** store each unit's cards in an envelope. Review lessons, bingo and the bonus games reuse them.
- **Not printable:** crayons, tape, and a pin or pencil for the weather wheel.

items.title: Lesson 1 – Hello and colors
items.body:
- **Goal:** say hello, say her name, recognize 4 colors.
- **New words:** red, blue, yellow, green
- **Key sentences:** "What's your name?" "My name is ___." "It's red."
- **Materials:** puppet, color cards, balloon coloring page, crayons, star chart.
**Print before class (4 pages, color):** color cards (red, blue, yellow, green), balloon coloring page, star chart and monkey puppet. The star chart and puppet are printed once and kept all term.
1. **Hello (5 min):** Teach the routine you will use all term: wave, hello chant, "How are you?" with a thumbs up, high five.
2. **Meet the puppet (5 min):** The puppet says "Hello! My name is ___. What's your name?" Whisper "My name is…" to help her answer. Repeat with the puppet acting shy, then loud, then sleepy.
3. **New words (10 min):** Hold up each card and say "Red. Red. Red." She repeats. Then lay all four out: "Point to blue!" "Give me yellow!"
4. **Color jump (15 min):** Spread the cards on the floor. "Jump on green!" Then "Touch something red!" and she runs to find something red in the room.
5. **Balloon coloring (10 min):** Point to a balloon and say "Color this balloon blue." Say it once; she listens and colors.
6. **Teacher swap (10 min):** She calls "Jump on ___!" and you jump. Make mistakes on purpose so she corrects you.
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** First sticker on the chart. "Goodbye! See you Saturday!"
**Home practice:** Ask "What color?" about her clothes and toys.

send.title: Hello and colors
send.notes:
New words: red, blue, yellow, green
Key sentences: "What's your name?" "My name is ___." "It's red."
send.homework: Ask "What color?" about her clothes and toys.

items.sectionIntro: By Lesson 8 she can introduce herself: her name, her age, how she feels and a color she likes. Unit 1 also gives her colors, numbers 1–10 and body words, which come back in every later lesson.

items.title: Lesson 2 – More colors
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 9 colors and answer "What color is it?"
- **New words:** orange, purple, pink, black, white
- **Key sentences:** "What color is it?" "It's pink."
- **Materials:** all 9 color cards, mystery bag with colored objects (crayons, toys, a fruit), paper, crayons.
**Print before class (1 page, color):** color cards for orange, purple, pink, black and white. Bring the Lesson 1 color cards too.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Fast flash (5 min):** Flash Wednesday's 4 colors quickly; she shouts each one. Then hide one card: "What's missing?"
3. **New words (10 min):** Teach the 5 new colors with loud, whisper and silly voices. Ask "What color is it?" and model "It's orange."
4. **Color corners (15 min):** Put a color card on each wall. Call a color; she runs there. Then change how she moves: hop, tiptoe, walk slowly.
5. **Mystery bag (10 min):** She pulls out an object. You ask "What color is it?" She answers "It's purple!" Then she draws her favorite object in its color.
6. **I spy colors (10 min):** "I see something… green!" She points to guess. Then she gives the clue and you guess.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** At meals, ask "What color is it?" about the food.

send.title: More colors
send.notes:

send.homework: At meals, ask "What color is it?" about the food.

items.title: Lesson 3 – Numbers 1–5
items.body:
- **Goal:** count to 5 and say her age.
- **New words:** one, two, three, four, five
- **Key sentences:** "How old are you?" "I'm six." "How many?" "Three!"
- **Materials:** number cards 1–5, small things to count (bottle caps, stones, beans), paper, crayons, puppet.
**Print before class (2 pages):** number cards 1–5 (color) and the count-and-color worksheet.
1. **Hello (5 min):** Add "How old are you?" to the routine from today. Show six fingers: "I'm six!"
2. **Color review (5 min):** Fast "Touch something pink!" round.
3. **New words (10 min):** Count fingers 1–5 together. Show the number cards, then count objects into a pile: "One, two, three…"
4. **Count and move (15 min):** "Jump three times!" "Clap five times!" "Spin two times!" Count out loud together every time.
5. **Count and color (10 min):** Draw rows of 1 to 5 circles. "Color two circles red." This mixes numbers and colors.
6. **Puppet's age (10 min):** The puppet asks "How old are you?" She answers. Then she asks the puppet, who gives a silly age: "I'm one hundred!" Finish with "How many?" questions about the objects.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Count stairs or plates together, 1 to 5.

send.homework: Count stairs or plates together, 1 to 5.

items.title: Lesson 4 – Numbers 6–10
items.body:
- **Goal:** count to 10 and answer "How many?"
- **New words:** six, seven, eight, nine, ten
- **Key sentences:** "How many red ones?" "Four!"
- **Materials:** number cards 1–10, chalk or tape for a hopscotch grid, colored objects to count, a soft ball.
**Print before class (1 page, color):** number cards 6–10. No chalk at the school? Lay all ten number cards on the floor as the hopscotch.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Finger numbers (5 min):** Hold up fingers; she says the number. Then she shows fingers and you say it.
3. **New words (10 min):** Count to 10 on fingers. Introduce cards 6–10. Line all ten up, mix them, and she puts them back in order.
4. **Number hopscotch (15 min):** Draw a 1–10 grid on the ground. She counts out loud as she hops. Then call "Jump on seven!"
5. **Count the colors (10 min):** Make a pile of mixed colored objects. "How many red ones?" She counts and answers.
6. **Ball count (10 min):** Throw the ball back and forth, counting catches to 10. Then she says a number and you clap that many times.
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** Tell her the next lesson is in two weeks if you are traveling.
**Home practice:** Count to 10 together every day during the break, and keep asking "What color?"

send.notes:

send.homework: Count to 10 together every day during the break, and keep asking "What color?"

items.title: Lesson 5 – My face
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 6 parts of the face.
- **New words:** eyes, nose, mouth, ears, hair, teeth
- **Key sentences:** "Touch your nose!" "This is my mouth."
- **Materials:** picture cards, paper plate or paper circle, crayons, yarn or paper strips for hair, glue, small mirror if you have one.
**Print before class (2 pages):** face cards (color) and a big empty face, which replaces the paper plate.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Big review after the break (10 min):** Mix colors and numbers: "Show me three fingers!" "Touch something white!" "How many blue crayons?"
3. **New words (10 min):** Point to your own face: "Nose. Nose. Nose." She touches hers and repeats. Use the mirror if you have one.
4. **Touch it fast (10 min):** "Touch your eyes! Touch your hair!" Speed up. Then combine: "Touch your ears and jump!"
5. **Paper-plate face (10 min):** "Draw two eyes. Draw one nose. Color the hair black." She follows your instructions; the numbers and colors come back.
6. **Silly puppet (10 min):** She tells the puppet "Touch your mouth!" The puppet touches its ear. She corrects it: "No! Mouth!" Then she points and says "This is my ___."
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** At bath or bedtime, ask "Where's your nose?"

send.notes:
New words: eyes, nose, mouth, ears, hair, teeth

send.homework: At bath or bedtime, ask "Where's your nose?"

items.title: Lesson 6 – My body
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 7 body parts and follow movement commands.
- **New words:** head, shoulders, knees, toes, arms, hands, feet
- **Key sentences:** "Simon says, touch your knees!" "Shake your hands!"
- **Materials:** picture cards, large paper (or a normal sheet), markers.
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of body cards (color) and a body outline to color, which replaces tracing her on big paper.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Face review (5 min):** Quick "Touch your ___" round with the face words.
3. **New words (10 min):** Touch each part on yourself and say it. Sing "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes" slowly, then fast.
4. **Simon says (15 min):** "Simon says, touch your knees!" If you don't say "Simon says," she must freeze. Add "Clap your hands" and "Stamp your feet."
5. **Body outline (10 min):** She lies on the large paper while you trace her (or draw a small body on a sheet). "Color the arms blue. Color the feet green."
6. **She's Simon (10 min):** She gives the commands to you. Encourage the full sentence: "Touch your head!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Sing "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes" together.

send.title: My body
send.notes:
New words: head, shoulders, knees, toes, arms, hands, feet
Key sentences: "Simon says, touch your knees!" "Shake your hands!"
send.homework: Sing "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes" together.

items.title: Lesson 7 – Feelings
items.body:
- **Goal:** say how she feels.
- **New words:** happy, sad, angry, scared, tired, hungry
- **Key sentences:** "How are you?" "I'm happy." "Are you sad?" "No!"
- **Materials:** feelings cards (simple drawn faces), paper circles, crayons, puppet.
**Print before class (2 pages):** feelings cards (color) and the feelings drawing page with 6 empty faces.
1. **Hello (5 min):** From today, she answers "How are you?" with a real feeling, not only a thumbs up.
2. **Body review (5 min):** A fast round of Simon says.
3. **New words (10 min):** Act out each card big: stomp for angry, yawn for tired, rub your tummy for hungry. She copies the face and says the word.
4. **Feelings walk (10 min):** "Walk like you're happy!" "Walk like you're tired!" Clap to make her freeze, then "Show me scared!"
5. **Draw the feelings (10 min):** She draws one face per feeling on paper circles. "Draw a sad mouth." Keep them for Lesson 8.
6. **Guess the feeling (15 min):** Act a feeling with no words; she guesses: "You're tired!" Swap roles. Then the puppet acts feelings and she names them.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** At dinner, ask "How are you?" and wait for a feeling word.

send.title: Feelings
send.notes:

send.homework: At dinner, ask "How are you?" and wait for a feeling word.

items.title: Lesson 8 – Review: All About Me
items.body:
- **Goal:** introduce herself in 4 short sentences.
- **New words:** none. One new chunk: "I like ___."
- **Key sentences:** "Hello! My name is ___. I'm six. I'm happy. I like pink."
- **Materials:** large paper for a poster, her feelings faces from Lesson 7, crayons, glue, all Unit 1 cards.
**Print before class (1 page):** the All About Me poster. Bring all the Unit 1 cards.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Quick-fire cards (10 min):** Mix cards from colors, numbers, face, body and feelings. Flash each one; she names it before you count to 3.
3. **Practice the introduction (10 min):** The puppet models it first. She practices one sentence at a time, then all four together.
4. **Card hunt (10 min):** Hide 10 cards around the room. She finds each one and names it before bringing it back.
5. **All About Me poster (15 min):** She draws herself in the middle, then adds 6 candles, her favorite color and a feelings face. You write the English labels.
6. **Present it (5 min):** She shows the poster to the puppet, or to a teacher at the school, using her four sentences. Big applause.
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** Fill in the Unit 1 checklist after the lesson.
**Home practice:** She shows the poster to her parents and introduces herself in English.

send.title: Review: All About Me
send.notes: Key sentences: "Hello! My name is ___. I'm six. I'm happy. I like pink."
send.homework: She shows the poster to her parents and introduces herself in English.

items.title: Lesson 9 – My family
items.body:
- **Goal:** name family members and say "This is my ___."
- **New words:** mom, dad, brother, sister, baby, grandma, grandpa
- **Key sentences:** "Who's this?" "This is my mom."
- **Materials:** family picture cards, paper, crayons, puppet plus 3–4 other toys as the puppet's family.
- **Note:** Teach only the family words that fit her family first; add the rest as "the puppet's family."
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of family cards (color) and the My Family drawing page.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Introduction review (5 min):** She says her four sentences from Lesson 8 to the puppet.
3. **New words (10 min):** Show each card and act it out: the baby cries, grandpa walks slowly. She repeats.
4. **Family statues (10 min):** "Walk like a baby!" (she crawls). "Walk like grandpa!" "Dance like dad!" Clap to make her freeze.
5. **Draw my family (15 min):** She draws her family. Point and ask "Who's this?" She answers "This is my ___." Finish with "How many people?"
6. **Toy family (10 min):** She introduces the puppet's toy family: "This is the baby. This is the grandma." Then the toys say hello to each other.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Parents point to family photos and ask "Who's this?"

send.notes:
New words: mom, dad, brother, sister, baby, grandma, grandpa
Key sentences: "Who's this?" "This is my mom."
send.homework: Parents point to family photos and ask "Who's this?"

items.sectionIntro: By Lesson 16 she can talk about the people, animals, food, clothes and weather around her. The three sentence patterns of this unit are "This is my ___," "I like ___" and "Can I have ___, please?"

items.title: Lesson 10 – Animals at home and on the farm
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 7 animals and their English sounds.
- **New words:** dog, cat, chicken, goat, cow, duck, fish
- **Key sentences:** "What's this?" "It's a dog." "The cow says moo."
- **Materials:** animal cards, toy animals if you have them, mystery bag, paper, crayons.
**Print before class (2 pages, color):** animal cards for dog, cat, chicken, goat, cow, duck and fish.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Family review (5 min):** Flash the family cards: "Who's this?"
3. **New words (10 min):** Show each card and make the English sound: woof, meow, cluck, baa, moo, quack, and blub-blub for the fish. Compare with French sounds; she will find it funny.
4. **Animal moves (15 min):** "Walk like a duck!" "Run like a dog!" "Swim like a fish!" Then make a sound; she acts the animal and names it.
5. **Mystery bag (10 min):** She feels a toy or card in the bag and guesses "It's a cat!" Then she draws one animal. Ask "What color is your cat?"
6. **Guess my animal (10 min):** She makes a sound; you guess "It's a goat!" Swap roles.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Name the animals you see outside: dogs, chickens, goats.

items.title: Lesson 11 – Wild animals
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 7 wild animals and say what she likes.
- **New words:** elephant, lion, monkey, snake, crocodile, bird, turtle
- **Key sentences:** "I like monkeys." "I don't like snakes."
- **Materials:** animal cards, a simple jungle drawing on paper, crayons.
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of wild animal cards (color) and the My Jungle drawing page.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Farm review (5 min):** You make a sound; she names the animal.
3. **New words (10 min):** Teach each with an action: arm trunk for the elephant, roar for the lion, hiss for the snake, snapping arms for the crocodile, very slow walk for the turtle. Tell her the elephant is the symbol of Côte d'Ivoire.
4. **Jungle walk (15 min):** Walk through an imaginary jungle. Shout an animal and she becomes it: "Crocodile!" and she snaps; "Turtle!" and she moves very slowly.
5. **My jungle picture (10 min):** "Draw a green snake. Draw two birds. Draw a big elephant."
6. **Like or don't like (10 min):** Show each card. She gives a thumbs up, "I like elephants!" or a thumbs down, "I don't like snakes!" Then she asks you: "Do you like lions?"
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Parents ask "Do you like monkeys?" She answers "Yes!" or "No!"

New words: elephant, lion, monkey, snake, crocodile, bird, turtle

send.homework: Parents ask "Do you like monkeys?" She answers "Yes!" or "No!"

items.title: Lesson 12 – Fruit
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 7 fruits and ask for one politely.
- **New words:** banana, mango, pineapple, orange, avocado, coconut, watermelon
- **Key sentences:** "Can I have a banana, please?" "Here you are." "Yummy!"
- **Materials:** real fruit from the market if possible, a knife for you only, plates, fruit cards, paper, crayons.
- **Note:** Check with her parents about food allergies before the tasting.
**Print before class (2 pages, color):** fruit cards.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Wild animal review (5 min):** Act an animal; she names it.
3. **New words (10 min):** Show the real fruit or cards. She touches, smells and repeats. Point out that orange is a color and a fruit.
4. **Fruit market run (10 min):** Put fruit cards around the room. "Bring me a pineapple!" She runs and gives it to you: "Here you are!"
5. **Fruit salad (15 min):** You cut small pieces. She asks "Can I have a mango, please?" before each piece and says "Yummy!" or "I don't like it." No real fruit? She draws and colors a fruit bowl.
6. **Fruit shop (10 min):** She sells, you buy: "Can I have two bananas, please?" She counts them out. Swap roles.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** At home or at the market, she asks "Can I have a mango, please?"

New words: banana, mango, pineapple, orange, avocado, coconut, watermelon

items.title: Lesson 13 – Food and drinks
items.body:
- **Goal:** name everyday food and drinks and order politely.
- **New words:** rice, bread, fish, chicken, egg, water, milk
- **Key sentences:** "I'm hungry!" "Can I have rice, please?" "Thank you!"
- **Materials:** food cards, paper plates and cups, magazines or drawings to cut out, child-safe scissors, glue, puppet.
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of food cards (color) and a plate template, which replaces the paper plates.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Fruit review (5 min):** Mystery bag with fruit or cards: "What's this?"
3. **New words (10 min):** Show each card and mime eating or drinking. Link it to Lesson 7: rub your tummy and say "I'm hungry!"
4. **Feed the puppet (10 min):** Spread cards on the floor. The puppet says "I'm hungry! I want fish!" She runs, picks the card and feeds it. Speed up.
5. **My plate (15 min):** She draws or glues her favorite meal on a paper plate. Ask "What's on your plate?" She answers "Rice and fish!"
6. **Restaurant (10 min):** She is the waiter: "Hello! What do you want?" You order: "Rice, please." Swap; she orders and says "Thank you!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** At meals she says "Can I have water, please?" and "Thank you."

items.title: Lesson 14 – Clothes
items.body:
- **Goal:** name 7 clothes and follow "Put on" and "Take off."
- **New words:** shirt, dress, shorts, pants, shoes, socks, hat
- **Key sentences:** "Put on your hat!" "Take off your shoes!" "My dress is pink."
- **Materials:** a bag of real clothes (big adult clothes are funnier), clothes cards, a paper doll outline, crayons, puppet.
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of clothes cards (color) and the paper doll page.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Food review (5 min):** A fast restaurant round: "Can I have ___, please?"
3. **New words (10 min):** Pull the clothes out of the bag and put them on yourself in silly ways. She repeats each word.
4. **Dress-up race (15 min):** "Put on the hat! Put on the big shoes!" She dresses up fast while you count to 10, then "Take off the hat!"
5. **Paper doll (10 min):** "Color the dress yellow. Draw a red hat. Draw blue socks."
6. **Fashion show (10 min):** She walks like a model and describes herself: "My hat is blue." You clap. Then she dresses the puppet: "Put on your shoes!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Getting dressed in English in the morning: "Put on your shoes!"

items.title: Lesson 15 – Weather
items.body:
- **Goal:** say what the weather is like.
- **New words:** sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot, cold
- **Key sentences:** "How's the weather?" "It's sunny!" "It's hot!"
- **Materials:** weather cards, a paper plate, a paper arrow and a pin or brass fastener, crayons, the clothes bag from Lesson 14.
**Print before class (2 pages, color):** weather cards and the weather wheel with its arrow. Bring a pin or pencil for the wheel's center.
1. **Hello (5 min):** Add "How's the weather?" to the routine. Look outside together.
2. **Clothes review (5 min):** A quick "Put on your ___!" round.
3. **New words (10 min):** Act each one: sunglasses for sunny, finger rain for rainy, fanning your face for hot, shivering for cold, swaying for windy. December harmattan days are a good real example of windy.
4. **Weather game (10 min):** "It's rainy!" and she hides under the table. "It's sunny!" and she dances. "It's windy!" and she spins. Speed up.
5. **Weather wheel (15 min):** She draws sun, rain, cloud and wind on the paper plate and you attach the arrow. Use it in every hello routine from now on.
6. **What do I wear? (10 min):** She spins the wheel: "It's rainy!" Then she dresses you from the clothes bag: "Put on your hat!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Every morning, ask "How's the weather?"

send.title: Weather
send.notes:
New words: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot, cold
Key sentences: "How's the weather?" "It's sunny!" "It's hot!"
send.homework: Every morning, ask "How's the weather?"

items.title: Lesson 16 – Review: My World
items.body:
- **Goal:** use all Unit 2 words in games and a short talk.
- **New words:** none.
- **Key sentences:** "This is my mom. I like mangoes. It's sunny."
- **Materials:** all Unit 2 cards, two 3 × 3 picture bingo grids, beans or stones as markers, a paper game board with 15 picture squares, a die, crayons.
**Print before class (3 pages, color):** 2 bingo boards on one page, the Picture race board game (landscape) and the My World drawing page. Use number cards 1–6 face down instead of a die. Bring all the Unit 2 cards.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Category sort (10 min):** Mix all the cards. She sorts them into piles: family, animals, food, clothes, weather. She names each card as she places it.
3. **Picture bingo (15 min):** Call a word; whoever has the picture covers it. She calls the second game.
4. **Board game race (10 min):** Roll the die, count the steps out loud in English and name the picture you land on.
5. **Draw my world (10 min):** She draws her family, a favorite animal, a favorite food and today's weather.
6. **Tell me about it (5 min):** She presents the drawing: "This is my mom. I like mangoes. It's sunny."
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** Fill in the Unit 2 checklist after the lesson.
**Home practice:** She explains her drawing to her parents in English.

send.title: Review: My World
send.notes: Key sentences: "This is my mom. I like mangoes. It's sunny."
send.homework: She explains her drawing to her parents in English.

items.title: Lesson 17 – Action words
items.body:
- **Goal:** do and say 7 actions, and say what she can do.
- **New words:** run, jump, walk, dance, sing, swim, sleep
- **Key sentences:** "Can you jump?" "Yes, I can!" "I can dance."
- **Materials:** action cards, music on your phone, animal cards from Lessons 10–11, paper, crayons.
**Print before class (2 pages, color):** action cards. Bring the animal cards from Lessons 10 and 11.
1. **Hello (5 min):** Spin the weather wheel.
2. **Weather review (5 min):** A short round of the weather game from Lesson 15.
3. **New words (10 min):** Do each action as you say it; she copies. Then say only the word and she does it without watching you.
4. **Freeze dance (10 min):** Play music while she dances. Stop it and call an action: "Jump!" "Sleep!" "Swim!" Go faster each round.
5. **What can it do? (10 min):** She picks an animal card and draws it doing something. Ask "What can it do?" Help her answer "The monkey can jump." Ask silly questions too: "Can a fish run?" "No!"
6. **I can show (15 min):** She shows you what she can do: "I can jump! I can sing!" Then she asks you "Can you swim?" and you answer and act it out.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Parents ask "Can you jump? Can you sing?" She answers "Yes, I can!" and shows them.

send.title: Action words
send.notes:
New words: run, jump, walk, dance, sing, swim, sleep
Key sentences: "Can you jump?" "Yes, I can!" "I can dance."
send.homework: Parents ask "Can you jump? Can you sing?" She answers "Yes, I can!" and shows them.

items.sectionIntro: Unit 3 adds action words, "I can ___" and "Where's the ___?", celebrates Christmas, and ends with a short English show for her parents.

items.title: Lesson 18 – Christmas
items.body:
- **Goal:** learn Christmas words and make a card for her parents.
- **New words:** Christmas tree, star, present, Santa Claus, bell, candle
- **Key sentences:** "Merry Christmas!" "Happy New Year!" "This is for you."
- **Materials:** Christmas picture cards, paper stars, colored paper, stickers or glitter, glue, a small wrapped present (a sweet or sticker inside), a bell if you have one.
- **Note:** If her family does not celebrate Christmas, make it a New Year lesson with present, star, party and "Happy New Year!"
**Print before class (3 pages):** Christmas cards (color), 8 stars for the star hunt, and the Christmas card to fold (landscape).
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Action review (5 min):** A short round of freeze dance.
3. **New words (10 min):** Show each card. Ring the bell. Hand her the wrapped present, but she keeps it closed until step 6.
4. **Star hunt (10 min):** Hide paper stars around the room and guide her with actions: "Walk… stop! Jump! Look!" She counts the stars she finds.
5. **Christmas card (15 min):** She folds paper and decorates it. "Draw a tree. Draw three presents. Color the star yellow." You write "Merry Christmas!" and she traces it.
6. **Give and open (10 min):** She practices giving the card to the puppet, then to a teacher: "Merry Christmas! This is for you!" Then she opens her present and says "Thank you!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** "Merry Christmas! Happy New Year! See you in January!"
**Home practice:** Over the break, she gives the card to her parents in English. Parents keep asking "How are you?" and "How's the weather?"

send.title: Christmas
send.notes:
New words: Christmas tree, star, present, Santa Claus, bell, candle
Key sentences: "Merry Christmas!" "Happy New Year!" "This is for you."
send.homework: Over the break, she gives the card to her parents in English. Parents keep asking "How are you?" and "How's the weather?"

items.title: Lesson 19 – Toys and in, on, under
items.body:
- **Goal:** name her toys and say where things are.
- **New words:** ball, doll, car, teddy bear, balloon, in, on, under
- **Key sentences:** "Where's the ball?" "It's under the table."
- **Materials:** her own toys (the lesson is at her home), a box, a table and chair, paper, crayons, puppet.
**Print before class (2 pages, color):** toy cards and the in, on, under cards.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Big review after the break (10 min):** Quick-fire cards from Units 1 and 2. Spend extra time on anything she has forgotten.
3. **New words (10 min):** She shows you her toys and you name them in English. Then use the ball and the box: "The ball is in the box. The ball is on the table. The ball is under the table."
4. **Hide the teddy (15 min):** She closes her eyes while you hide the teddy. "Where's the teddy?" When she finds it, help her say "It's under the bed!" Swap roles.
5. **Draw the room (10 min):** "Draw a table. Draw a ball under the table. Draw a cat on the table."
6. **Puppet's lost toys (5 min):** The puppet asks "Where's my car?" She answers "It's in the box!"
7. **Goodbye (5 min):** Tell her Saturday is her English show.
**Home practice:** Tidy up in English: "Put the doll in the box."

send.title: Toys and in, on, under
send.notes:
New words: ball, doll, car, teddy bear, balloon, in, on, under
Key sentences: "Where's the ball?" "It's under the table."
send.homework: Tidy up in English: "Put the doll in the box."

items.title: Lesson 20 – Show what you know
items.body:
- **Goal:** show her parents what she has learned, and celebrate.
- **New words:** none.
- **Materials:** her folder of work, the posters from Lessons 8 and 16, a homemade "English Star" certificate, stickers, music.
- **Before the lesson:** Invite her parents for the last 15 minutes, or a teacher at the school if they can't come.
**Print before class (1 page):** the certificate (landscape), in color if you can.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Rehearse the show (15 min):** Five short parts: her introduction, counting to 10, "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes," three sentences about her world, and an "I can" action.
3. **Favorite games (15 min):** She picks her two favorite games of the term. It warms her up before the show.
4. **Certificate (5 min):** She colors the border of her certificate.
5. **The show (15 min):** She performs for her parents. Then she teaches them a game, such as Simon says, in English.
6. **Goodbye (5 min):** Last sticker, the certificate, and a big round of applause.
**After the lesson:** Fill in the Unit 3 checklist. Anything not ticked becomes the review for next term's first lessons.

items.title: Bonus A – Shapes and sizes
items.body:
- **New words:** circle, square, triangle, star, heart, big, small
- **Key sentences:** "It's a big circle." "Find a square!"
- **Materials:** paper shapes in different colors and sizes, glue, paper.
**Print before class (3 pages):** 2 pages of shape cards (color) and a page of shapes to color and cut out.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Review (5 min):** The last lesson's words.
3. **New words (10 min):** Draw each shape in the air with her, then on paper. Show a big and a small one of each.
4. **Shape hunt (15 min):** Find shapes in the room: the window is a square, the clock is a circle. "Find a triangle!"
5. **Shape picture (10 min):** She builds a house or robot from paper shapes: "Glue a big triangle. Glue two small squares."
6. **Describe it (10 min):** She describes the pieces of her picture: "It's a small red circle."
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**

send.title: Shapes and sizes
send.notes:
New words: circle, square, triangle, star, heart, big, small
Key sentences: "It's a big circle." "Find a square!"

items.sectionIntro: Use these on extra dates, over the holidays, or whenever she needs a fun catch-up. Bonus A fits any time after Lesson 4; B and C fit any time.

items.title: Bonus B – Story day
items.body:
- **Goal:** enjoy a short English picture book and act it out.
- **Book ideas:** "Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See?" (colors and animals) or "The Very Hungry Caterpillar" (numbers and food). No book? Make a 4-page one together.
- **Materials:** the book, the puppet and toys, paper folded into a mini book, crayons.
**Print before class (1 page):** the mini book template (landscape). Fold it in 8, cut the marked middle line, and fold it into a book.
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Review game (5 min).**
3. **Picture walk (10 min):** Look at the pictures before reading. She names everything she knows: colors, animals, numbers.
4. **Read aloud (10 min):** Read slowly with actions. Pause before familiar words so she can finish them.
5. **Act the story (15 min):** Act it out with the puppet and toys. She plays the main role.
6. **My mini book (10 min):** She draws one page each for "I like…" and you write the words. She "reads" it back to you.
7. **Goodbye (5 min).**

items.title: Bonus C – Game day
items.body:
- **Goal:** mixed review of everything learned so far.
- **Materials:** all picture cards, a soft ball, a pair of each card for memory.
**Print before class (1 page, color):** the memory game, 16 small cards (8 pairs).
1. **Hello (5 min).**
2. **Card slap (10 min):** Spread cards on the table. Call a word; the first to slap the card wins it.
3. **Memory pairs (15 min):** Cards face down. She names every card she turns over, even when it isn't a match.
4. **Ball questions (10 min):** Toss the ball with a question: "How old are you?" "What color is your dress?" "Do you like fish?" She answers and throws it back with a question for you.
5. **Treasure hunt (15 min):** Hide 8 cards. Give clues in English: color and number clues early in the term, "It's under the chair" after Lesson 19.
6. **Goodbye (5 min).**

items.title: Progress checklists
items.body:
Tick each item after the unit's review lesson. Anything not ticked goes into the review step of the next lessons.

### Unit 1 (after Lesson 8)
- Answers "What's your name?" with "My name is ___."
- Answers "How old are you?" with "I'm six."
- Names at least 7 of the 9 colors
- Counts to 10 without help
- Touches the right face or body part when you name it
- Says how she feels: "I'm happy," "I'm tired," "I'm hungry"
- Introduces herself in 4 short sentences

### Unit 2 (after Lesson 16)
- Says "This is my ___" about her family
- Names at least 10 animals
- Says "I like ___" and "I don't like ___"
- Asks "Can I have ___, please?" and says "Thank you"
- Names at least 5 clothes and follows "Put on your ___"
- Answers "How's the weather?"

### Unit 3 (after Lesson 20)
- Says "I can ___" with at least 4 actions
- Answers "Can you ___?" with "Yes, I can!" or "No"
- Says "Merry Christmas!" and "Happy New Year!"
- Answers "Where's the ___?" using in, on or under
- Performs her show for her parents

courses.title: Adults: beginner English
courses.about: 10 weekly lessons in 3 units (Hello and me, Everyday life, At the airport and review), plus 2 bonus lessons and a Unit 1 quiz.

items.title: How the lessons work
items.body:
10 lessons for adult beginners whose main language is French. Each lesson runs over one week in two one-hour classes: the first for the new language, the second for listening and role-play. It starts from zero and stays in the present tense. Every lesson ends with one or two airport sentences, for a learner who works at an airport.

### The lesson routine (two 60-minute classes)
Every lesson follows the same steps over its two classes. There's no break in a one-hour class, so keep each activity short. Each lesson below tells you what to do in each step.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up chat (5 min).** Same opening every class: "Good evening! How are you?" "I'm fine, thank you. And you?" Add one new question each week.
2. **Homework check and review (10 min).** Go over the homework, then a quick game with last week's words.
3. **New language (25 min).** 8–12 new words and a few phrases. Say each one; they repeat three times together, then alone, then read it on the handout. Explain any grammar in French in a sentence or two.
4. **Practice together (15 min).** Cards, games and simple questions, husband and wife asking each other.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min).** Each says one new thing they learned. Give a small task for Thursday.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up chat (5 min).**
2. **Quick review (10 min).** Monday's words and phrases in a fast game.
3. **Listening (15 min).** A short dialogue (5–8 lines) read three times: first they just listen, then you act it out, then they read along. Simple questions; one-word answers are fine.
4. **Real-life role-play (20 min).** A situation they'll really meet, using the week's phrases. Then swap roles.
5. **Airport sentences (5 min).** He practices the week's airport sentences; she plays the traveler.
6. **Wrap-up and homework (5 min).** The homework is on the back of the handout.

### Phrases to teach on day one
These four are on the Lesson 1 handout with the French, so they never need French to ask: Repeat, please. Slowly, please. I don't understand. How do you say ___ in English?

### Tips for teaching French-speaking adults
- They're true beginners. Explain each activity in French first, then do it in English.
- Phrases before grammar. "What's your name?" is learned as one block long before they know why it works.
- Say every word before they read it. English spelling doesn't follow the sounds the way French does.
- Recycle. Every lesson reuses the greetings, numbers and questions from before.
- Fix the classic French-speaker mistakes gently:
    - "I have 35 years" → "I'm 35."
    - "His" and "her" follow the owner: "his wife," "her husband."
    - "You like rice?" → "Do you like rice?"
- Pronunciation to watch: the "h" in hello, "th" in thank you, and the letters E / I and G / J.
- With a couple, ask each person by name so the stronger one doesn't answer for both. Nobody wants to look bad in front of their spouse.
- At 19:30 they've already worked a full day. Start light, keep them talking, and change activity every 10–15 minutes.
- Praise every try. In the first weeks understanding is the goal; speaking comes slowly.

### Materials kit (make once, reuse all term)
- **A notebook each,** split into three parts: words, grammar, homework.
- **The board** at the school, and markers.
- **Scissors and an envelope per unit** for the printed cards, so each unit's set stays together.
- **Your phone** to record dialogues and for WhatsApp voice notes.
- **A folder** for their written work and the progress checklists.

### Printing
Every lesson has its own file, named like "Lesson 03 printables.pdf." Print it a day or two before Monday's class. The bottom of each page says how many copies to print.
- **Handouts:** two sides per lesson: words and phrases with the French on the front, exercises and homework on the back. One copy each, printed double-sided (or two pages stapled).
- **Teacher pages:** the listening scripts, questions with answers, the handout answer key and the checklists. One copy for you.
- **Cards, maps and props:** cut on the dashed lines. Keep the airport map from Lesson 7; Lesson 9 uses it again.
- **Paper size:** A4. If your printer uses Letter paper, choose "Fit to page."
- **Color:** everything works in black and white. The play money, maps and certificates look nicer in color.
- **Total:** 60 sheets for Lessons 1–10, plus 4 for the bonus lessons.

### Homework
Plan on about 15 minutes a day, 5 days a week. Each week has two parts:
- **Writing:** the back of the handout, given on Thursday and brought on Monday.
- **Speaking:** a 30-second WhatsApp voice note to you in English. Reply with a voice note too; it's the best practice between lessons.

items.title: Lesson 1 – Hello!
items.body:
- **Goal:** greet people, say their name, ask someone's name, count to 10.
- **New words:** hello, hi, good morning, good afternoon, good evening, goodbye, yes, no, please, thank you, sorry; numbers 0–10.
- **Phrases:** "What's your name?" "My name is ___." "Nice to meet you." "How are you? I'm fine, thank you. And you?"
- **Grammar:** none yet. "I'm" is learned inside the phrases.
- **Airport:** "Good evening. Welcome to Abidjan." "Have a good evening!"
**Print before class (4 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), number cards, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** Say hello with a big wave and your name. Then explain in French how the classes work: two a week, a handout, homework, voice notes.
2. **What do you know? (10 min):** Ask in French which English words they already know. Write every one on the board and praise it. Teach the four classroom phrases.
3. **New language (25 min):** Greetings: draw a rising sun, a high sun and a moon on the board. Then "What's your name? My name is…" and "Nice to meet you," shaking hands as you say it.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** Numbers 0–10 on fingers, then with the number cards: you say, they point; they say, you point.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** Each says hello, their name and goodbye. For Thursday: greet each other in English at home.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** Teach "How are you? I'm fine, thank you. And you?"
2. **Review (10 min):** Number cards, fast. Then greetings by time of day.
3. **Listening (15 min):** Awa and Konan meet (teacher page). Read it three times and ask the four questions.
4. **Role-play (20 min):** A party: each greets you, says their name, asks yours, asks how you are and says goodbye. Then they meet each other.
5. **Airport (5 min):** He stands at a "door": "Good evening. Welcome to Abidjan." She answers "Thank you!" He says "Have a good evening!" Then swap.
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Say hello, good evening and goodbye in English every day. Count from 0 to 10 in English.

send.notes:

items.sectionIntro: By Lesson 4 they can greet people, say their name, age, phone number, where they're from and what they do, and talk about their family. That's enough for a first real conversation.

items.title: Lesson 2 – Letters and numbers
items.body:
- **Goal:** spell their names, count to 100, give their phone number and age.
- **New words:** the alphabet; numbers 11–100.
- **Phrases:** "How do you spell it?" "What's your phone number?" "How old are you? I'm 35."
- **Grammar:** to be: I am, you are, he is, she is. "I'm 35," never "I have 35 years."
- **Airport:** "Your gate is number 4." "Your seat is 12A."
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided, with a French sound hint for each letter), alphabet chart for the wall, number bingo, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** "Good evening! How are you?"
2. **Review (10 min):** Number cards 0–10, names and greetings.
3. **New language (25 min):** The alphabet with the wall chart; drill E / I and G / J. Then "How do you spell it?" They spell their names.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** Spelling race from the teacher page: you spell, they write; then they spell for you.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** For Thursday, practice spelling their names.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Spell a few words. Then numbers 11–20 and the tens (30, 40… 100).
3. **Listening (15 min):** Phone numbers and ages from the teacher page. They write what they hear.
4. **Role-play (20 min):** Number bingo, then "What's your phone number? How old are you?" with each other and you.
5. **Airport (5 min):** Gate and seat numbers: "Your gate is number 4. Your seat is 12A."
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Spell the names of 3 family members in English. Write their phone number in English words.

items.title: Lesson 3 – Where are you from? What do you do?
items.body:
- **Goal:** say where they're from and what they do, and introduce their spouse.
- **New words:** Côte d'Ivoire / Ivorian, France / French, the USA / American, Ghana / Ghanaian, Nigeria / Nigerian, Senegal / Senegalese; teacher, driver, nurse, doctor, student, shop owner, businessman, airport agent.
- **Phrases:** "Where are you from? I'm from Côte d'Ivoire." "What do you do? I work at the airport." "This is my wife. Her name is ___."
- **Grammar:** to be with we and they; "Are you…? Yes, I am. / No, I'm not."
- **Airport:** "Can I see your passport, please?" "Where are you flying to?"
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), party cards, practice passports, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** Welcome them back.
2. **Review (10 min):** Spell your name, phone number, age.
3. **New language (25 min):** Countries on a phone map: the country, then the nationality. Jobs with mime; they guess.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** Party cards: each takes one and answers "Where are you from? What do you do?"
5. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Mime a job; they say it.
3. **Listening (15 min):** Grace and Daniel (teacher page), three times, four questions.
4. **Role-play (20 min):** A party with the cards, then as themselves. Each introduces their spouse: "This is my wife. Her name is…"
5. **Airport (5 min):** She fills in a practice passport; he asks for it and where she's flying to.
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** A voice note: "Hello, my name is… I'm from… I work at…"

items.title: Lesson 4 – My family + Unit 1 check
items.body:
- **Goal:** talk about their family, and introduce themselves in 5 sentences.
- **New words:** husband, wife, daughter, son, child / children, father, mother, parents, brother, sister, grandfather, grandmother.
- **Phrases:** "Do you have children? Yes, I have one daughter." "Who's this? This is my brother. His name is ___."
- **Grammar:** I have, she has; my, your, his, her. His and her follow the owner, not the thing.
- **Airport:** "Please wait here." "One moment, please." "Thank you for waiting."
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), family tree ×2, listening tree ×2, teacher page with the Unit 1 checklist.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** "Where are you from? What do you do?"
3. **New language (25 min):** Family words with your own family on the board. Then they listen to your family and fill in the listening tree. Teach his and her slowly.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** Each fills in their family tree; the other asks "Who's this? What's his name?"
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** Thursday is a friendly check; they learn their 5 sentences from the back of the handout.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Family photos on their phones: "Who's this?" "This is my…"
3. **Unit 1 check (35 min):** About 15 minutes alone with each person (teacher page). Tick the Unit 1 checklist. Meanwhile the other writes their 5 sentences.
4. **Airport (5 min).**
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** One thing each does well, one thing to work on.
**Home practice:** Show a family photo to someone and say "This is my…" in English.

Grammar: I have, she has; my, your, his, her. His and her follow the owner, not the thing.

items.title: Unit 1 quiz
items.body:
A 20-minute written quiz for the Unit 1 check (Lesson 4, second class), marked out of 40. The instructions are in French. Print the quiz once per student from the Claude doc "Unit 1 Quiz – Hello and me"; this page is your copy with the answers.

### How to run it
1. Do Part 1 together at the start of the Unit 1 check (3 min): read the listening script below.
2. While you do the oral check alone with one person (about 15 min), the other does Parts 2–10. Then swap.
3. Part 10 is their 5 sentences, so it replaces the "write your 5 sentences" task in the lesson.
4. Mark it at home and give it back at the next class, with one thing each did well.

### The quiz
**Part 1 – Listen and write (4 points).** _Écoutez et écrivez._ Two numbers, a name spelled out, and a phone number.

**Part 2 – Greetings (3 points).** _Complétez avec morning, afternoon ou evening._ 08:00 – Good …! · 15:00 – Good …! · 20:00 – Good …!

**Part 3 – Questions and answers (5 points).** _Entourez la bonne réponse._
1. How are you? a) I'm fine, thank you. And you? b) My name is Aya. c) I'm from Ghana.
2. How old are you? a) I have 35 years. b) I'm 35. c) I'm a nurse.
3. Where are you from? a) I'm a driver. b) Nice to meet you. c) I'm from Côte d'Ivoire.
4. What do you do? a) I work at the airport. b) I'm fine, thank you. c) I'm Ivorian.
5. Do you have children? a) Yes, I am. b) This is my son. c) Yes, I have one daughter.

**Part 4 – Countries and nationalities (4 points).** Word box: American · French · Senegalese · Ivorian. Côte d'Ivoire, France, the USA, Senegal (example: Nigeria → Nigerian).

**Part 5 – Jobs (4 points).** Word box: student · nurse · shop owner · doctor · businessman · driver. un chauffeur, une infirmière, un médecin, un commerçant (example: un enseignant → teacher).

**Part 6 – My family (4 points).** Word box: sister · grandfather · mother · daughter. father → … · son → … · brother → … · grandmother → … (example: husband → wife).

**Part 7 – am, is or are? (4 points).** I … from Côte d'Ivoire. · My husband … a driver. · We … Ivorian. · You … my teacher.

**Part 8 – his or her? (4 points).** This is my husband. … name is Konan. · This is my sister. … name is Grace. · Aya has one son. … son is 10. · Daniel has a wife. … wife is a nurse.

**Part 9 – At the airport (3 points).** Sentences: Please wait here. · Your gate is number 4. · Good evening. Welcome to Abidjan. · Can I see your passport, please? Situations: a traveler arrives in the evening; you want to see the passport; the traveler must wait.

**Part 10 – About me (5 points).** Five sentences: My name is… · I'm… (age) · I'm from… · I work at… / I'm a… · I have… (family)

### Listening script (Part 1)
Read each one twice, slowly.
1. "Number one: fourteen."
2. "Number two: forty."
3. "Number three: my name is Grace. G – R – A – C – E."
4. "Number four: my phone number is oh seven – two three – one five – six oh – eight four."

Fourteen and forty are a deliberate pair: stress four-TEEN and FOR-ty so they can hear the difference.

### Answer key
| Part | Answers | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Listening | 14 · 40 · GRACE · 07 23 15 60 84 | 4 |
| 2 Greetings | morning · afternoon · evening | 3 |
| 3 Questions | 1 a · 2 b · 3 c · 4 a · 5 c | 5 |
| 4 Nationalities | Ivorian · French · American · Senegalese | 4 |
| 5 Jobs | driver · nurse · doctor · shop owner | 4 |
| 6 Family | mother · daughter · sister · grandfather | 4 |
| 7 am / is / are | am · is · are · are | 4 |
| 8 his / her | His · Her · Her · His | 4 |
| 9 Airport | Good evening. Welcome to Abidjan. · Can I see your passport, please? · Please wait here. | 3 |
| 10 About me | Their own sentences: 1 point each | 5 |
| **Total** |  | **40** |

### Marking tips
- One small spelling slip ("Senegales") still gets the point. Write the correct spelling next to it.
- Part 1: the phone number needs all 10 digits, and the name all 5 letters, for the point.
- Part 10: 1 point per clear, correct sentence. "I have 35 years" gets no point; write "I'm 35." beside it. A model answer: "My name is Konan. I'm 40. I'm from Côte d'Ivoire. I work at the airport. I have one daughter."
- Part 3 question 2 and Part 8 test the two classic French-speaker mistakes. If either is wrong, add it to the review in Lesson 5.

### What the score means
- **34–40:** Unit 1 is solid. Move on to Unit 2.
- **26–33:** Good. Go over the parts with mistakes in Lesson 5's review step.
- **Under 26:** Add a short Unit 1 game to the review step of Lessons 5 and 6, and praise what they got right.

items.title: Lesson 5 – Time and my day
items.body:
- **Goal:** tell the time, say the day, and say what time they do things.
- **New words:** Monday to Sunday, today; morning, afternoon, evening, night; o'clock, thirty; get up, go to work, eat, come home, go to bed.
- **Phrases:** "What time is it? It's seven o'clock." "What day is it today? It's Monday." "What time do you get up? I get up at five."
- **Grammar:** present simple with I and you: "I get up at five." "What time do you…?"
- **Airport:** "Boarding is at nine o'clock." "Your flight is on time." "Your flight is delayed."
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), routine cards ×2, clock to cut out, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** Add a new question: "What day is it today?"
2. **Review (10 min):** Family: "Do you have children? What's your wife's name?"
3. **New language (25 min):** Days of the week. Then the time with the clock, only o'clock and thirty this week: "seven o'clock," "seven thirty."
4. **Practice together (15 min):** You set the clock, they say the time; then they set it and you say it.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** For Thursday, note what time they get up and go to bed.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** "What day is it today? What time is it?"
2. **Review (10 min):** The clock, fast.
3. **Listening (15 min):** Your day (teacher page). They write the time next to each activity.
4. **Role-play (20 min):** With the routine cards: "What time do you get up?" "I get up at five." Each puts the cards in order for their own day and says it.
5. **Airport (5 min):** With a boarding pass: "Boarding is at nine o'clock. Your flight is on time." Then "Your flight is delayed."
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Every morning, say the day and the time in English.

items.sectionIntro: By Lesson 8 they can tell the time, buy food and ask prices, ask for directions in town and at the airport, and say what they like.

items.title: Lesson 6 – Food and money
items.body:
- **Goal:** name food, ask prices, and buy or order politely.
- **New words:** rice, bread, fish, chicken, meat, eggs, tomatoes, water, juice, fruit, attiéké; hundred, thousand, francs; cheap, expensive.
- **Phrases:** "How much is it? It's 1,000 francs." "I'd like rice, please." "Here you are." "That's expensive!"
- **Grammar:** "I'd like…" learned as a phrase.
- **Airport:** "How many bags do you have?" "One bag." "Would you like some water?"
**Print before class (6 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), price list and menu ×2, play money ×2, market cards, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** The clock and the days.
3. **New language (25 min):** Food with pictures or real food. Then big numbers for prices: 100, 500, 1,000, 2,500, 10,000.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** You say a price, they write it; they say one, you write it. Then "How much is…?" with the price list.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Food words with the price list.
3. **Listening (15 min):** At the restaurant (teacher page), three times, four questions.
4. **Role-play (20 min):** The market with the play money and cards, then the restaurant with the menu. You're the waiter first.
5. **Airport (5 min):** "How many bags do you have?" "Would you like some water?"
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Name 5 foods in English at one meal. Write a shopping list in English.

items.title: Lesson 7 – Where is it? Town and airport
items.body:
- **Goal:** ask where places are and give simple directions, in town and at the airport.
- **New words:** bank, pharmacy, hospital, market, school, hotel, toilets, taxi; left, right, straight; next to, opposite.
- **Phrases:** "Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?" "Go straight. Turn left. It's next to the bank." "Thank you!" "You're welcome."
- **Grammar:** "Where is…?" "Is there a…? Yes, there is."
- **Airport:** "Check-in is on the left." "The toilets are on the right." "Taxis are outside." "Go straight, then turn left."
**Print before class (6 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), town map ×3, airport map ×2 (keep it for Lesson 9), airport cards, teacher page.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Prices: "How much is the rice?"
3. **New language (25 min):** Places on the town map. Left, right and straight with your body; next to and opposite with objects on the table.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** "Where is the bank?" on the map. They answer: "It's next to the pharmacy."
5. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Simon says with directions: "Turn left! Go straight!"
3. **Listening (15 min):** Three short routes on the town map (teacher page). They follow with a finger and say where they are.
4. **Role-play at the airport (25 min):** With the airport map, she's a traveler asking for check-in, the toilets, a gate and the taxis; he answers. Then swap.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** A voice note: the way from their house to the market ("Go straight, turn left…").

items.title: Lesson 8 – Likes + Unit 2 check
items.body:
- **Goal:** say what they like, ask "Do you like…?", and use all of Unit 2 in a conversation.
- **New words:** football, music, cooking, dancing, the beach, TV, shopping; love, like, don't like.
- **Phrases:** "Do you like football? Yes, I do. / No, I don't." "I love music." "I don't like fish." "How was your weekend? It was good!"
- **Grammar:** "Do you like…?" and short answers.
- **Airport:** review every airport sentence so far.
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), activity cards, survey ×2, teacher page with the Unit 2 checklist.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** Teach "How was your weekend? It was good!" as a phrase.
2. **Review (10 min):** Directions on the town map.
3. **New language (25 min):** Activities with the cards and mime. Love, like and don't like with thumbs. Then "Do you like…? Yes, I do. / No, I don't."
4. **Practice together (15 min):** The survey: they ask each other and you.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** Thursday is a friendly check.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Unit 2 check (40 min):** About 18 minutes alone with each person (teacher page): the time, buying food, directions, likes. Tick the Unit 2 checklist. Meanwhile the other does the back of the handout.
3. **Airport review (10 min):** He says every airport sentence so far; she answers as the traveler.
4. **Wrap-up (5 min).**
**Home practice:** Ask each other "Do you like…?" three times a day.

items.section: Unit 3 – At the airport, and review (Lessons 9–10)
items.title: Lesson 9 – At the airport
items.body:
- **Goal:** him: handle simple airport situations in English. Her: say 5 sentences about her own job.
- **New words:** passport, boarding pass, ticket, flight, gate, check-in, security, bag, delayed, on time; her own 6–8 work words.
- **Phrases:** his 12 airport sentences (on the handout); "Merry Christmas!" "Happy holidays!"
- **Grammar:** polite phrases: "Can I see…, please?" "Please wait here."
**Print before class (5 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), boarding passes and passport, role cards, teacher page. Bring the airport map from Lesson 7.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Every airport sentence from Lessons 1–8.
3. **New language (25 min):** Airport words with the boarding pass and the map. Then her job: ask her in French what she says at work, and give her the English.
4. **Practice together (15 min):** Polite or rude? "Passport!" becomes "Can I see your passport, please?"
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** For Thursday, she writes her 5 work sentences.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Review (10 min):** Fix her 5 sentences until she can say them without reading.
3. **Listening (15 min):** Two short announcements (teacher page). They write the flight, the gate and the time.
4. **Role-play (25 min):** Check-in, a delayed flight and directions to the gate, with the props. Then her job, with him as the customer.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** "Merry Christmas! Happy holidays!" and the holiday homework.
**Home practice (over the holidays):** He says his 12 airport sentences every day; she says her 5 work sentences. A voice note to you with holiday wishes in English.

items.sectionIntro: Lesson 9 puts all his airport English together and gives her English for her own job. Lesson 10 reviews the whole term and ends with a final conversation.

items.section: Unit 3 – At the airport, and review (Lessons 9–10)
items.title: Lesson 10 – Big review + final conversation
items.body:
- **Goal:** use everything from the term, and show what they've learned.
- **New phrases:** "Happy New Year!" "How were the holidays? They were good!"
**Print before class (5 pages):** review handout (2 copies, double-sided, all the term's key phrases with the French), quick-fire cards, teacher page with the Unit 3 checklist, certificates.
**Monday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** "Happy New Year! How were the holidays?"
2. **Review game (20 min):** Quick-fire cards: pick a card, answer it, then ask the other.
3. **Stations (25 min):** Five short role-plays in a row: meeting someone, a family photo, "What time is it?", the market, directions.
4. **Airport run-through (5 min).**
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** Thursday is the final conversation; the review handout is their study sheet.
**Thursday (60 min)**
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Final conversation (30 min):** About 15 minutes alone with each person, no notes (teacher page). Tick the Unit 3 checklist.
3. **Couple's role-play (15 min):** You're a visitor: first at the airport with him, then as a guest at their home. They greet you, introduce each other, offer a drink and say what they like.
4. **Wrap-up (10 min):** Certificates. Ask what they want next term: more airport English, the past tense to tell stories, phone calls.
**After the lesson:** Anything not ticked on the checklists becomes the review in next term's first lessons.

send.notes: Key sentences: "Happy New Year!" "How were the holidays? They were good!"

items.title: Bonus A – Health basics
items.body:
- **New words:** head, stomach, tooth, back, throat; sick, headache, stomachache, fever, medicine, doctor, pharmacy.
- **Phrases:** "I'm sick." "I have a headache." "Where is the pharmacy?" At the airport: "Are you OK? Do you need a doctor?"
**Print before class (3 pages):** handout (2 copies, double-sided), teacher page with the role cards.
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **New language (20 min):** Body words by pointing, then the problems with mime.
3. **Practice together (10 min):** One mimes a problem; the other says "You have a headache!"
4. **Listening (10 min):** The pharmacy dialogue (teacher page), three times.
5. **Role-play (10 min):** At the pharmacy. Then the airport: a traveler is sick, and he asks "Are you OK? Do you need a doctor?"
6. **Wrap-up (5 min).**

items.title: Bonus B – Game day
items.body:
- **Goal:** speak as much as possible with what they already know. No new language.
**Print before class (1 page):** question cards. Reuse the number bingo from Lesson 2 and the market from Lesson 6 if you have them.
1. **Warm-up (5 min).**
2. **Question cards (20 min):** They take turns picking a card, answering it, then asking the other the same question.
3. **Number bingo (10 min).**
4. **Party role-play (20 min):** You're a guest at their home. They welcome you and make small talk. In December, make it a Christmas party.
5. **Wrap-up (5 min):** Go over the mistakes you noted, and give each person one phrase to use more.

courses.title: Kids 6–7: 3-month plan
courses.about: 24 lessons over 12 weeks in 3 months, with a game bank and a progress tracker.

items.title: How the lessons work
items.body:
24 one-hour lessons over 12 weeks for a 6-year-old beginner whose main language is French: one lesson at school introduces a theme, the next at home practices it with her own things. Lessons are numbered, not dated, so if one is missed, pick up at the next number.

### Every lesson follows the same routine
| Minutes | Part | What happens |
| 0–5 | Hello | Same hello song and puppet greeting every time; "How are you?" |
| 5–12 | Review | One quick game with the last lesson's words |
| 12–25 | New words | 4–6 new words, with cards or real objects and a gesture for each |
| 25–40 | Play | One active game using the new words (see Game bank) |
| 40–52 | Make | Coloring, craft or worksheet; she says the words while she works |
| 52–60 | Goodbye | Recap the words, sticker on her chart, goodbye song, take-home task |
At 6, she'll focus for about 10 minutes at a time. Switch activities as soon as she gets restless, even if it's earlier than planned.

### Saturday vs Wednesday
- Saturday at school: a board, space to move, fewer distractions. Best for new words, movement games and letter sounds.
- Wednesday at home: her toys, kitchen, clothes and family photos become your teaching materials, and her parents see what she's learning.

### Tips for a French-speaking 6-year-old
- Stay in English with gestures, pictures and mime. Use a quick word of French only to explain a game's rules.
- Expect French sound habits: a dropped "h" (hello, happy), "th" said as "z" or "s" (three, this), and stress on the last syllable. Repeat the word correctly back to her rather than correcting her.
- In the first weeks, pointing and acting out count as success. Speaking comes after lots of listening.
- She's likely learning to read in French right now, so keep English reading light: letter sounds and tracing only.
- A puppet that "only speaks English" gets shy kids talking.

### Materials to prepare
Get the first five ready before lesson 1. Each lesson lists exactly what to print and cut. Cards are hard paper cut into 4 (about postcard size), with a simple drawing on the front and the English word on the back.
- A hand puppet with an English name (a sock puppet works)
- A folder or notebook for her "My English Book": every coloring page and craft goes in it
- Sticker sheet and a reward chart with 24 squares, one per lesson
- Crayons or colored pencils, glue, child-safe scissors
- A soft ball (or rolled-up socks)
- Phone or speaker for songs: search YouTube for each song title in the lessons
- Month 1 flashcards: feelings, colors, numbers 1–10, body parts
- Month 2 flashcards: family, animals, fruit and food, clothes
- Month 3 flashcards: toys, actions, weather, days of the week, party words
- A big die, paper plates, chalk or paper squares for floor games
- Real objects where possible: fruit, toy animals, doll clothes
- An alphabet chart for the classroom wall
- A simple certificate for lesson 24

items.title: Lesson 1 – Hello, my name is…
items.body:
_Saturday at school_

Prep · Print: a 24-square sticker chart (or draw one). Cut: 10 cards for the level check (cat, dog, apple, ball, mom, red, blue, 1, 2, 3).
- 0–5 min · Hello: the puppet waves and says "Hello! My name is…"
- 5–15 min · Teach: hello, goodbye, yes, no, "What's your name?", "My name is…". Wave for hello and goodbye, nod and shake your head for yes and no.
- 15–25 min · Play: ball toss; whoever catches says "My name is…"
- 25–35 min · Level check: show the 10 cards one by one and note which she can name. Don't correct, just note.
- 35–47 min · Make: decorate the cover of her "My English Book" with her name.
- 47–52 min · Yes/no game: hold up a card and ask "Is this a dog?"
- 52–60 min · Goodbye: first sticker on her chart, goodbye wave. Home: show her parents the hello and goodbye waves.

send.title: Hello, my name is…
send.notes: New words: hello, goodbye, yes, no, "What's your name?", "My name is…"
send.homework: Show her parents the hello and goodbye waves.

items.sectionIntro: By lesson 8 she can greet you, say her name and age, name 10 colors, count to 10 and name 10 body parts.

items.title: Lesson 2 – How are you?
items.body:
_Wednesday at home_

Prep · Print: nothing. Cut: 5 feeling cards (happy, sad, tired, hungry, angry) and 1 big circle for the face craft.
- 0–5 min · Hello: puppet greeting.
- 5–12 min · Review: ball toss with names, then the yes/no game.
- 12–25 min · Teach: happy, sad, tired, hungry, angry; "How are you?" "I'm happy." Show each card with a big face and body mime, then you make a face and she names it.
- 25–40 min · Play: Simon Says with stand up, sit down, look, listen, clap.
- 40–52 min · Make: draw a happy face on one side of the circle and a sad face on the other.
- 52–60 min · Goodbye: sticker. Home: she asks each family member "How are you?"

send.title: How are you?
send.notes: New words: happy, sad, tired, hungry, angry; "How are you?" "I'm happy."
send.homework: She asks each family member "How are you?"

items.title: Lesson 3 – Six colors
items.body:
_Saturday at school_

Prep · Print: a rainbow coloring page and an A–C letter tracing sheet. Cut: 6 blank cards (she colors them into her color cards).
- 0–5 min · Hello.
- 5–12 min · Review: "How are you?" with the feeling cards.
- 12–25 min · Teach: red, blue, yellow, green, black, white; "It's red." Use crayons and things in the classroom.
- 25–40 min · Play: "Touch something red!" She runs to it, then she gives the orders.
- 40–47 min · Make: she fills each blank card with one color. That's her color deck.
- 47–52 min · Letter sounds: alphabet song, then trace A (apple), B (ball), C (cat).
- 52–60 min · Goodbye. Home: rainbow coloring page, and a color hunt for one thing of each color.

send.title: Six colors
send.notes: New words: red, blue, yellow, green, black, white; "It's red."
send.homework: Rainbow coloring page, and a color hunt for one thing of each color.

items.title: Lesson 4 – What color is it?
items.body:
_Wednesday at home_

Prep · Print: an Ivorian flag outline (or draw a rectangle split in 3). Cut: 4 blank cards for the new colors.
- 0–5 min · Hello.
- 5–12 min · Review: she names her color hunt finds, then flashcard slap with her color cards.
- 12–25 min · Teach: orange, pink, purple, brown; "What color is it?" Use her toys and clothes.
- 25–40 min · Play: I spy with colors around the house.
- 40–52 min · Make: she colors the 4 new cards, then the Ivorian flag (orange, white, green).
- 52–60 min · Goodbye. Home: name the color of what she wears each morning.

send.title: What color is it?
send.notes: New words: orange, pink, purple, brown; "What color is it?" Use her toys and clothes
send.homework: Name the color of what she wears each morning.

items.title: Lesson 5 – Count to 10
items.body:
_Saturday at school_

Prep · Print: a count-and-color worksheet (1–10) and a D–F tracing sheet. Cut: 10 number cards (the digit plus that many dots) and 10 paper squares for hopscotch, or use chalk.
- 0–5 min · Hello.
- 5–12 min · Review: flashcard slap with the color cards.
- 12–25 min · Teach: one to ten with fingers, then claps and jumps ("Jump 3 times!").
- 25–40 min · Play: number hopscotch; call a number, she jumps on it.
- 40–47 min · Make: count-and-color worksheet.
- 47–52 min · Letter sounds: D (dog), E (egg), F (fish).
- 52–60 min · Goodbye. Home: count the steps or stairs at home.

send.title: Count to 10
send.notes: New words: one to ten with fingers, then claps and jumps ("Jump 3 times!")
send.homework: Count the steps or stairs at home.

items.title: Lesson 6 – How many? How old?
items.body:
_Wednesday at home_

Prep · Print: a birthday cake coloring page (or draw one). Cut: nothing new; bring the number cards.
