items.title: Game bank
items.body:
All games work with one child. Let her play the teacher often; kids love giving the orders.
| Game | How to play one-on-one | Good for |
| Simon Says | Give commands; she moves only if you say "Simon says" first. Swap roles. | Commands, body, clothes, actions |
| Ball toss | Throw a soft ball with a question; she answers when she catches it. | Names, feelings, any question |
| Flashcard slap | Lay out 4–6 cards, say a word, she slaps the right card. | Any new words |
| Touch something… | Call a color or object; she runs to touch it. | Colors, classroom, home |
| I spy | "I spy something blue"; she guesses, then she spies. | Colors, home objects |
| What's missing? | 5–6 cards or toys in a row; she closes her eyes, you remove one, she names it. | Any theme |
| Memory pairs | Pairs of cards face down; say the word for each card you turn over. | Review |
| Charades | Act out a word; the other guesses. Take turns. | Animals, actions, feelings |
| Teacher makes mistakes | Say the wrong word on purpose; she corrects you. | Confidence, any theme |
| Hot and cold | Hide an object; guide her with "hot" and "cold". | Toys, where things are |
| Number hopscotch | Numbers on the floor; she jumps on the one you call. | Numbers |
| Market | Shop with real or paper food: "A mango, please." "Here you are." | Food, polite words |
| Freeze dance | Music on; stop it and call an action or word. | Actions, burning off energy |

items.title: Progress tracker
items.body:
Tick each item when she does it without help. Check at lessons 8, 16 and 24, as a game rather than a test.

### Month 1 (lesson 8)
- Says hello, goodbye and "My name is…"
- Answers "How are you?" with a feeling
- Follows stand up, sit down, look, listen
- Names 8 or more colors
- Counts to 10 and says "I'm six"
- Names 8 or more body parts

### Month 2 (lesson 16)
- Introduces her family: "This is my mom"
- Names 8 or more animals
- Names 8 or more foods and says "I like… / I don't like…"
- Asks politely: "A mango, please"
- Names 5 or more clothes with a color: "a blue shirt"

### Month 3 (lesson 24)
- Uses in, on and under
- Says "I can… / I can't…"
- Describes the weather
- Says the days of the week
- Sings the alphabet song and knows the first sound of 10 or more letters
- Performs the show for her parents

### Parent update (after lessons 8, 16 and 24)
Keep it to three lines, in whichever language the parents prefer:
1. What she can do now (from the ticked list above).
2. One thing to practice at home this month, such as colors at breakfast or counting steps.
3. One song or phrase the family can use with her every day.

courses.title: Preschool 3–5: a year of English
courses.about: 30-minute weekly classes for petite, moyenne and grande section, one theme a month from October to June.

items.title: How the lessons work
items.body:
Three 30-minute classes on the same day: petite section (about 3 years old), moyenne section (about 4) and grande section (about 5). All three follow the same monthly theme, so you plan one lesson a week and adjust it for each level. Each month covers songs, counting, colors or everyday things through a theme the children can see, touch and act out.

| Section | Age | By June they should be able to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Petite section | about 3 | Sing along with actions, point to the right picture when they hear a word, count 1 to 5 with you |
| Moyenne section | about 4 | Say most theme words on their own, name 8 colors, count 1 to 10 |
| Grande section | about 5 | Answer simple questions ("What color is it?", "How many?"), use short phrases like "It's red", count 1 to 10 and recognize the written numbers |

### The 30-minute routine
Use the same six steps every week, in every section. Young children settle faster when they know what comes next.

| Time | Step | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–3 min | Hello | Same hello song every week, then greet each child: "Hello, Awa!" |
| 3–7 min | Review | Show last week's flashcards. Children say the word or point to it. |
| 7–14 min | New words | Show each word with a flashcard, a real object and a gesture. Say it 3–4 times, then the class repeats. |
| 14–20 min | Song | Sing the month's song with actions. |
| 20–27 min | Game or activity | A movement game, then a short table activity if there's time. |
| 27–30 min | Goodbye | Quick run through the new words, then the same goodbye song every week. |

Pick one hello song and one goodbye song from YouTube (Super Simple Songs and Dream English have short ones) and keep them all year. Download songs to your phone in advance in case there's no connection.

### Adapting it for each level
- **Petite section:** 3 new words a week. They listen, point and do the actions; don't expect much speaking yet. Change activity every 3–5 minutes.
- **Moyenne section:** 4 new words a week. Ask them to say each word back, and give simple choices: "Is it red or blue?"
- **Grande section:** 5 new words a week plus one short phrase ("It's a cat", "I like mangoes"). Ask questions and let children take turns being the teacher with the flashcards.

items.title: Year at a glance
items.body:
One theme per month, October to June. Petite section learns the first 3 words of each list, moyenne section about 6, and grande section all of them plus the phrase.

| Month | Theme | Words | Grande section phrase | Songs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| October | Hello & colors | hello, goodbye, red, blue, yellow, green | "It's red." | Hello song, goodbye song, "I See Something Blue" |
| November | Numbers 1–5 | one, two, three, four, five | "How many?" "Three!" | "Five Little Ducks", "Five Little Monkeys" |
| December | My body | head, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, hands, feet, knees, toes | "This is my nose." | "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes", "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" |
| January | Animals | dog, cat, chicken, cow, goat, duck, fish | "It's a dog." | "Old MacDonald Had a Farm" |
| February | More colors & shapes | orange, pink, circle, purple, black, white, square, triangle | "It's a red circle." | Color song, a shapes song |
| March | Numbers 6–10 | six, seven, eight, nine, ten | "I have ten fingers." | "Seven Steps", "One, Two, Buckle My Shoe" |
| April | Fruits & food | banana, mango, orange, pineapple, apple, water, bread, rice | "I like mangoes." | "Apples and Bananas" |
| May | Family | mommy, daddy, baby, brother, sister, grandma, grandpa | "This is my mommy." | "Finger Family" |
| June | Weather, clothes & show | sun, rain, hat, hot, shoes, shirt | "It's sunny." | "Rain, Rain, Go Away", review of all songs |

Each month runs the same way: week 1 introduces the words, week 2 adds the song, week 3 is a game, week 4 is review and a craft. If a week falls on a holiday, drop week 4. In months with a fifth week, make it a fun day with every song learned so far.

items.title: Week 1: Hello!
items.body:
**Words:** hello, goodbye. Grande section adds "My name is ___."
1. **Hello (5 min):** Bring out your puppet. It waves and says "Hello!" to each child, and they wave back.
2. **New words (7 min):** The puppet "falls asleep." Children wake it up by shouting "Hello!" When it waves "Goodbye!" and sleeps again, they wave too. Repeat 4–5 times.
3. **Song (6 min):** Teach the hello song. Wave on every "hello."
4. **Game (7 min):** Sit in a circle and pass a ball. Whoever holds it says "Hello!" Grande section says "Hello! My name is Awa." Petite section can just wave.
5. **Goodbye (5 min):** Teach the goodbye song. The puppet waves goodbye to each child.

The first lesson is mostly about teaching the routine. Try to learn a few names in each section.

send.title: Hello!
send.notes: Words: hello, goodbye. Grande section adds "My name is ___."

items.sectionIntro: Four full lessons for the first month. Use them as a model for every month after.

items.title: Week 2: Red and blue
items.body:
**Words:** red, blue. Moyenne and grande add yellow. Grande section practices "It's red."
1. **Hello (3 min):** Hello song and greetings.
2. **Review (4 min):** The puppet says hello and goodbye. Children answer.
3. **New words (7 min):** Show a red flashcard and a red object, say "Red!" and repeat. Do the same with blue. Point to red and blue things in the classroom.
4. **Song (6 min):** Teach the color song.
5. **Game (7 min):** Stick red and blue paper on two walls. Call a color and children walk or run to touch it.
6. **Goodbye (3 min):** Hold up each card one last time, then the goodbye song.

For grande section, end the game by holding up a card and asking "What color is it?" They answer "It's red."

send.title: Red and blue
send.notes: Words: red, blue. Moyenne and grande add yellow. Grande section practices "It's red."

items.title: Week 3: Yellow and green
items.body:
**Words:** yellow, green, plus review of red and blue. Grande section practices "It's yellow."
1. **Hello (3 min):** Hello song and greetings.
2. **Review (4 min):** "Show me red!" Children point to the right card or something in the room.
3. **New words (7 min):** Introduce yellow and green the same way as last week.
4. **Song (6 min):** Color song, now with four colors.
5. **Game (7 min):** Color sorting. Spread mixed bottle caps or paper squares on the floor. Children sort them into piles by color. Petite section hands you the color you call out.
6. **Goodbye (3 min):** Quick color review, then the goodbye song.

send.title: Yellow and green
send.notes: Words: yellow, green, plus review of red and blue. Grande section practices "It's yellow."

items.title: Week 4: Color review and craft
items.body:
**Words:** all four colors, hello and goodbye.
1. **Hello (3 min):** Hello song and greetings.
2. **Review (5 min):** Magic bag. Slowly pull a colored object out of a bag while children shout the color.
3. **Song (5 min):** Color song.
4. **Game (8 min):** Traffic light. Children walk or dance around. Hold up green for "go," yellow for "slow" and red for "stop." Grande section children take turns holding the cards and saying the color.
5. **Craft (6 min):** Children color a simple balloon or rainbow sheet using the four colors. Ask "What color?" as you walk around.
6. **Goodbye (3 min):** Goodbye song.

If the month has a fifth week, make it a fun day: sing every song, play their favorite game, and repeat the traffic light.

items.title: November: Numbers 1–5
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section one to three. Moyenne and grande one to five. Grande adds "How many?" "Three!"
- **Week 1:** Count fingers, claps and jumps together. "Clap three times!"
- **Week 2:** Teach "Five Little Ducks" with fingers as the ducks.
- **Week 3:** Number jumping. Hold up a number card and children jump that many times.
- **Week 4:** Act out "Five Little Monkeys." Five children are the monkeys and the class counts them down.

items.sectionIntro: Each week follows the 30-minute routine. Below is what changes: the words, the song and the main game.

items.title: December: My body
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section head, eyes, nose. Moyenne adds mouth, ears, hands. Grande adds feet, knees, toes and "This is my nose."
- **Week 1:** "Touch your nose!" Children touch each body part as you say it.
- **Week 2:** Teach "Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes." Sing it slowly, then faster.
- **Week 3:** Teacher says. "Teacher says touch your ears!" Petite section just copies you.
- **Week 4:** Draw a face together, then sing "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" before the Christmas break.

items.title: January: Animals
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section dog, cat, chicken. Moyenne adds cow, goat, duck. Grande adds fish and "It's a dog."
- **Week 1:** Show animal flashcards and make each animal's sound together.
- **Week 2:** Teach "Old MacDonald Had a Farm." Each verse, a child picks the next animal card.
- **Week 3:** Animal walk. Call an animal and children move like it: waddle like a duck, hop like a chicken.
- **Week 4:** Guess the animal. You make the sound and they name it. Grande answers "It's a cow."

items.title: February: More colors & shapes
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section orange, pink, circle. Moyenne adds purple, black, white. Grande adds square, triangle and "It's a red circle."
- **Week 1:** New colors with paper squares, mixed in with October's colors.
- **Week 2:** Draw shapes in the air with your finger, then find circles in the classroom.
- **Week 3:** Shape hop. Draw shapes on the floor in chalk. Call one and children jump onto it.
- **Week 4:** Glue paper shapes into a picture, like a house or a sun. Grande describes it: "a yellow circle."

items.title: March: Numbers 6–10
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section reviews one to five. Moyenne and grande learn six to ten. Grande adds "I have ten fingers."
- **Week 1:** Count fingers to ten. Petite section counts to five with you.
- **Week 2:** Teach "Seven Steps," walking one step per number.
- **Week 3:** Number hunt. Hide number cards around the room. Children find one and say it.
- **Week 4:** Teach "One, Two, Buckle My Shoe" and count classmates together.

items.title: April: Fruits & food
items.body:
**Words:** Petite section banana, mango, orange. Moyenne adds pineapple, apple, water. Grande adds bread, rice and "I like mangoes."
- **Week 1:** Bring real fruit if you can. Children touch, smell and name it.
- **Week 2:** Teach "Apples and Bananas."
- **Week 3:** Pretend market. Grande asks "A banana, please" and says "Thank you." Petite hands you the fruit you name.
- **Week 4:** Mix fruit with colors: "The banana is yellow." Drop this week if it falls in the Easter break.

items.body:
**Words:** Petite section mommy, daddy, baby. Moyenne adds brother, sister. Grande adds grandma, grandpa and "This is my mommy."
- **Week 1:** Family flashcards. Act out a crying baby, a mommy rocking it, a daddy waving.
- **Week 2:** Teach "Finger Family" with one finger per person.
- **Week 3:** Children draw their family. Grande presents: "This is my daddy."
- **Week 4:** Review with a family guessing game using the flashcards.

items.body:
**Words:** Petite section sun, rain, hat. Moyenne adds hot, shoes, shirt. Grande adds "It's sunny" and "It's raining."
- **Week 1:** Weather words with gestures. Look outside and say what the weather is.
- **Week 2:** Dress-up bag with a hat, shoes and a shirt. "Put on your hat!" Teach "Rain, Rain, Go Away."
- **Weeks 3–4:** Each section practices two or three favorite songs to perform for parents at the end of the year.

items.title: Materials
items.body:
Most of this is cheap or free, and you reuse it all year. Ask the school what they already have (crayons, paper, glue) before buying anything.
- **A hand puppet or sock puppet:** the class friend who only speaks English. Little kids will talk to a puppet before they talk to you.
- **Flashcards:** one per word, drawn or printed on cardboard, about half a page each. Make each month's set before the month starts.
- **Colored paper squares:** red, blue, yellow and green first, then orange, pink, purple, black and white in February.
- **Small colored objects:** bottle caps, plastic cups, balls or bits of fabric for sorting and the magic bag.
- **A bag or box:** for the magic bag game.
- **A soft ball:** for passing games.
- **Your phone and a small speaker:** with every song downloaded in advance.
- **Chalk:** for drawing shapes on the floor in February.
- **Simple coloring sheets:** for craft weeks. Petite section needs big, simple shapes.

items.title: Teaching tips
items.body:
Keep it short, physical and the same every week.
- **Stay in English.** Use gestures, pictures and actions so children understand without translation. Switch to French only for safety or a quick instruction.
- **Move often.** Petite section can focus for 3–5 minutes, grande section up to 7–8. Change activity before they get restless, not after.
- **Use the same signals.** A clap pattern means "listen," hands up means "stop." Teach them in week 1 and use them every class.
- **Praise in English.** "Good job!", "Great!", "High five!" They'll pick these up quickly.
- **Don't force shy children to speak.** Pointing and doing the actions is real learning at this age.
- **Write two lines after each class.** Note which words each section struggled with and review them first thing the next week.

items.title: The past tense: how it works
items.body:
### How to use it
Most of the verbs people use every day are irregular, so learn the first table before the second. Verbs are listed roughly from most to least common.
- **Past simple** is for finished actions: _I went to the market yesterday._
- **Past participle** follows have / has / had and the passive: _I have gone. It was taken._
- For regular verbs, both forms are the same (_worked_, _worked_).

### Spelling rules for -ed
Most verbs just add -ed; four small rules cover the rest.
| Rule | Example |
| Most verbs: add -ed | work → worked |
| Ends in -e: add -d | live → lived |
| Consonant + y: change y to -ied | study → studied |
| Vowel + y: add -ed | play → played |
| Short verb ending consonant-vowel-consonant: double the last letter | stop → stopped, plan → planned |
| Never double w, x or y | fix → fixed, snow → snowed |

### Pronouncing -ed
The -ed ending adds an extra syllable only after a t or d sound. Saying "walk-ed" or "play-ed" is the most common mistake for French speakers.
| Sound | When | Examples |
| /t/ | After voiceless sounds: p, k, s, sh, ch, f, x | stopped, worked, washed, watched |
| /d/ | After voiced sounds and vowels | played, lived, called, opened |
| /ɪd/ (extra syllable) | After t or d | wanted, needed, started, decided |
Quick test: put your hand on your throat and say the last sound of the base verb. If you feel a buzz, it's /d/; no buzz, it's /t/.

### The verbs
The 60 irregular and 44 regular verbs are ready as word lists: open **Word lists** in the Library and tap **Add to Words**.
